essence: It is affection's logic: leap over being and non-being to the third (1); find freedom contagious among the unfree (2); take remembrance as medicine (3); crown Him moon-umbrella king (4); beg one glance (5); interrogate one's own dryness (6); mark unmelted hearts contemptible (7); make heart-union the vessel of powers (8); let meditation flood joys and sorrows alike (9); never part, more than self (10); roar and dance arrival (11); cancel other knowables and yogas (12); let Śiva-sound chase sorrows (13); deny any second great person (14); shrink the ocean to a play-lake by servitude (15); shame miseries by manifestation (16); recite inside supremacy (17); tie the knot of being-non-being (18); face the unseen all-pervading brightness (19); find the knower inside the known (20); and close crying sharp in knowing bewilderment (21).

sections.SUMMARY: It is affection's logic: leap over being and non-being to the third (1); find freedom contagious among the unfree (2); take remembrance as medicine (3); crown Him moon-umbrella king (4); beg one glance (5); interrogate one's own dryness (6); mark unmelted hearts contemptible (7); make heart-union the vessel of powers (8); let meditation flood joys and sorrows alike (9); never part, more than self (10); roar and dance arrival (11); cancel other knowables and yogas (12); let Śiva-sound chase sorrows (13); deny any second great person (14); shrink the ocean to a play-lake by servitude (15); shame miseries by manifestation (16); recite inside supremacy (17); tie the knot of being-non-being (18); face the unseen all-pervading brightness (19); find the knower inside the known (20); and close crying sharp in knowing bewilderment (21).
sections.FUNCTION: Love-song as metaphysics: affection (*praṇaya*) does it argument cannot — demanding, dancing, and bewildered by turns — so that the hardest doctrines (third beyond being, knower-in-known) arrive as lovers' speech, not theses.
sections.KEY TERMS:
* **tṛtīya** — the third: leap-target beyond the being/non-being pair; it's method in one word.
* **praṇaya** — affection with demand-rights: love that asks, not love that adores from afar.
* **samāveśa-absent** — immersion never named here (contrast Stotra 1, v.7); it works by affection, not by technique-words.
* **akṣamālā** — the rosary (v.17): practice continuing inside supremacy.
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Third song: after foundation (Stotra 1) and litany (Stotra 2), the first intimate address — the second person throughout. Read aloud as the turn from praise to love-talk.
sections.EXPLANATION: It alternates demand and doctrine. Verses 1–2 set the leap and its carriers: over the pair to the third; freedom contagious from the Free. Verses 3–5 are medicine, crown, and begging: remembrance cures, the moon-umbrella reigns, one glance is begged. Verses 6–8 interrogate and invert: why am I dry (6); the unmelted deserve contempt (7); heart-meeting makes gods' vessels (8). Verses 9–11 flood, bind, and celebrate: meditation drowns feelings equally (9); lifers never part (10); arrival proved by roaring (11). Verses 12–14 cancel and crown: no other knowable, no other yoga (12); sorrows flee sound (13); no second person (14). Verses 15–17 shrink, shame, and keep reciting: ocean to lake (15), miseries shamed by manifestation (16), rosary inside supremacy (17). Verses 18–20 tie the metaphysical knot openly and face its consequence: being-non-being-formed (18), unseen all-brightness (19), knower-in-known as supremacy's ground (20). Verse 21 refuses to untie anything: enough other cries; sharp crying in knowing bewilderment.
sections.BOUNDARY: HOW the leap of v.1 is made is unexplained — affection is the how, and affection is not analyzed. Verse 8's goddesses, verse 17's rosary-pointing, and verse 18's knot stand unresolved. v.7's contempt persuades; it does not exclude — do not systematize it against v.15's universal servitude.
sections.RELATED:
* Stotra 1, v.16 (the deceit) — the localization its everywhere-look (v.20) answers.
* Stotra 2, v.24 (embracers over knowers) — the same anti-method, in love's register.
* Stotra 13, v.5 (things-as-they-stand) — the perception its glance (v.5) begs for.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of affection (praṇaya); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the third beyond being/non-being. The rasa is the love-song as metaphysics — affection does the work argument cannot: demanding, dancing, bewildered by turns. The hardest doctrines (third beyond being, knower-in-known) arrive as lovers' speech, not theses. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śṛṅgāra: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as beloved.
